The TTD isn't "official" until then, but chances of it changes at this point are pretty low. Yea, Tim's notes would be best this time 🙂 Thanks <@360491619402776577> <@301186049323958275> > Note: TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY was reassessed and confirmed on All Core Devs on 2022/8/18. Consensus spec: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/releases/tag/v1.2.0-rc.3 Thanks for explaining the details! So around 30TH/s drop we see on mainnet would correspond to this. Luckily, it put us right on track to hit the TTD at Sep 15 The a10 asic drop may be temporary though as inno just has to release an update to fix it. Do they have a patch for the price of ETH too 😆 Looks at the title of this channel Hashrate/price correlation joke Apparently Ethermine stopped including Tornado transactions since a week. https://pbs.twimg.com/media/FafvpOWXkAA-6ue?format=jpg&name=medium Damn so that’s the first example of eth censoring an entity I think? <@354681205842771973> bitfinex is next! I’ve always said the next step of mev is for exchanges to pay to block competitors and for entities on eth to pay protection fees and it looks like this is the first step towards that. Interesting to see how ethermine hashrate changes with this then. Does miners have the same censorship ethos as the protocol? Or do they not care? Given the circumstances of mining ending in a month or so, even if they did care, I don't think they'd bother switching pools so close to the end, that creates another problem of potentially not mining enough on another pool to hit the payout threshhold pre-merge. That being said, if I still had hashrate and eth wasn't on the verge of censoring PoW itself, I'd be off them ASAP, but it'd prob take me longer to actually search for a non-censoring pool than to actually switch the hashrate. But that also being said, I would wager the vast majority of small individual miners don't know or care, and would stick with ethermine as they're basically the mining pool equivalent of coinbase. what do you mean "censoring PoW itself"? It's still a sign of things to come though. If Bitfly isn't including tornado txs on ethermine, safe to assume they won't on their ethpool staking service either right out of the gate. Oh come on, you know exactly what I mean. I'd just being cheeky. I do not know what you mean Don't think too hard about it. I wonder if binance pool is including them? As far as I'm aware that's the only other company that is currently doing both mining and staking pools. actually i think there's also f2pool/stakefish looks like f2pool is still including them Does anything say that pools must include the most profitable transactions in their blocks? It would only be censored if they started to uncle other pool's blocks for including these transactions. There's no ommers in PoS Good blog on technical nuances: <https://blog.bitmex.com/ofac-sanctions-ethereum-pos-some-technical-nuances/> Attestations are really the far more interesting part here. It's safe to say OFAC does not currently ponder the nuances of PoS algorithms.
